chapter: Glen Gray band: Red Nichols and Bobby Hackett
title: Nichols works his way up the trumpet section
summary: Nichols started on fourth trumpet to rebuild his lip while younger wartime trumpeters guarded their parts.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So what Red told me, what he wanted to do, he wanted to play fourth trumpet. He says, 'I want to get my lip in shape, and give me the fourth trumpet part. That's enough.' We had four trumpets and -- four trumpets, four trombones -- big bands in those days.

So Red starts in the band, and we were playing at the Sherman, and I'd go over sometimes. I was staying at the Sherman. And I'd go downstairs. I'd hear Red down in the musicians' room. He was practicing his long, low tones, getting his embouchure back, you know, and he would sit in the band, and play his part.
And he had it all planned. And this was fine; however, after about three, four weeks or maybe six weeks or so, his lip is in pretty good shape. Now he wants the third parts.

Now, trumpet players in those days, you -- you know that these kids during the war, they got to be -- before the war they got to be fantastic. They had guys like Louis Armstrong to look back on. Now they were fluffing him off, and Harry James, those guys were getting passé. These kids were coming along and they could play twice as high and probably twice as fast, and they had fantastic commands of their instruments, and the only thing that they worried about, most of them being 4-Fs, is the fact that they'd be pulled in the Army, got out of the band. So they wanted to show off as

Now, you take a part, even a fourth part, away from some kid because usually you gave him a solo now and then, and he'd get up and blow his brains out for that 16 or 32 bars because he, you know, "this is my chance."

So Red's coming in. He's creeping in. Then he creeps up into the third part. Then he wanted to get to the second part, and, you know, he couldn't play the high ones. So he would be satisfied with the second part, but he wanted some lead.

And by this time I could give him, as far as an arranger, I could give him a few things to do, to utilize his talents. But he was -- you know, he wanted it done more quickly. Well, how -- how long does it take to make an arrangement for -- put him in a spot -- when you got 14 or 13 other guys that you have to --
